records.title: Demand for grant of Scheduled Tribe status to Valmiki community of Tamil Nadu.
details:
Dr. M. Thambi Durai: 
The Valmiki community in Tamil Nadu has been
consistently seeking inclusion in the Scheduled Tribe list owing to its socio-economic
and educational backwardness and the need for the constitutional safeguards and
welfare benefits available to Scheduled Tribes. The demand has remained pending
for several years, causing widespread concern and uncertainty among the members
of the community. The proposal has already undergone examination at
various stages. The Government of Tamil Nadu has recommended the inclusion of
the Valmiki community in the Scheduled Tribe list, and the Ministry of Tribal
Affairs has processed the proposal through the prescribed procedure. At
present, the proposal is pending with the Registrar General of India (RGI)
under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The delay in completing the examination has
caused hardship to the community, which continues to await a final decision. I,
therefore, urge the? Government to expedite the examination of the proposal and
complete the process at the earliest in accordance with the established
procedure. An early decision on this long-pending matter would advance
the constitutional principles of social justice, equality and inclusive
development, while addressing the legitimate aspirations of the Valmiki
community of Tamil Nadu
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over coastal erosion and protection measures in Tamil Nadu.
details:
Dr. M. Thambidurai: I draw attention of
the Government to the serious and escalating problem of coastal erosion in
Tamil Nadu. The State has a long coastline of over 1,000 kilometers, and
significant portions are experiencing rapid erosion due to climate change,
rising sea levels, cyclones and extreme weather events. Coastal districts such
as Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Thoothukudi, Ramanathapuram and Chennai are facing
continuous shoreline retreat, resulting in loss of valuable land, damage to
houses, public infrastructure and fishing harbours, and severe threats to the
livelihoods of thousands of fisherfolk families. Many vulnerable villages are
witnessing displacement, saline water intrusion and destruction of roads and
community assets. Despite periodic studies and limited protective works such as
seawalls and groynes, the implementation of comprehensive, long-term coastal
management strategies remains inadequate and uneven. I urge the Government to
undertake a fresh, scientific and district-wise vulnerability assessment; substantially
enhance financial assistance under coastal protection schemes; expedite pending
projects; and adopt nature-based solutions such as mangrove restoration and
beach nourishment. A dedicated, time-bound Coastal Resilience Plan for Tamil
Nadu may be formulated in coordination with the State Government.? Coordinated
intervention is essential to protect vulnerable communities, secure critical
infrastructure and ensure sustainable development along Tamil Nadu?s coastline.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over influence of online gaming.
details:
Dr. M. Thambidurai: I draw
attention of the Government to a recent tragic and disturbing incident reporteda
Society in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, where three minor sisters aged 16, 14 and
12 died by suicide. Preliminary reports indicate that online digital obsession
they were unable to overcome. Police and media sources have indicated that the
sisters were deeply involved in an online task-based gaming application. Attempts
by their parents to restrict mobile phone usage allegedly resulted in increased
emotional distress among the minors. This heartbreaking incident recalls
earlier dangerous online challenges, which reportedly encouraged self-harm
among vulnerable adolescents.While investigations are ongoing, the tragedy
exposes serious gaps in digital safety, parental awareness and regulatory
oversight. ??????????? This is a national wake-up call. I urge the Government
to strengthen regulations, ensure age verification, promote digital literacy,
expand mental health support and integrate digital safety education in schools.
The safety and mental well-being of our children must remain paramount
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand for inclusion of Valmiki Community in the list of Scheduled Tribes(STs) in Tamil Nadu.
details:
Dr. M. Thambidurai: The Centre has been
adding the vulnerable communities in the List of STs or SCs in each State,
depending on the characteristics, after examining the same. I would like to
point out that there is a demand to include the Valmiki Community in the List
of STs in Tamil Nadu. This demand has been pending for a long time. This
Community is already included in the List of STs in the State of Karnataka. The
State of Tamil Nadu is an adjacent State and it is fit and proper that this
Community is included in the List of ST in Tamil Nadu. The people of the community
had met a former Chief Minister and made the representation to include them in
the category of Scheduled Tribes.? The Tribal Research Centre, Ooty had been
directed to examine it. It concluded that the Valmiki Community possesses five
distinctive tribal characteristics, namely, primitive traits, distinct culture,
shyness of contact, geographical isolation and social or economic backwardness
and recommended that they be included in the list of Scheduled Tribes. Several
measures were taken at the ground level, but final inclusion of this Community
in the ST List could not be achieved. Hence, it is requested that the Centre
may take action to include Valmiki Community in the List of STs in Tamil Nadu. 
????????? (ENDS)

records.title: very important matter afflicting the country, making lives of the people miserable, which is drug / alcohol menace.
details:
Dr.
M. Thambidurai: Sir,
I would like to raise a very important matter afflicting the country, making
lives of the people miserable, which is drug alcohol menace. Drug / alcohol
abuse has become a worldwide menace. This has emerged as a serious concern,
adversely affecting the physical and socio-economic well-being of the country.
The epidemic of drug abuse in younger generation has assumed alarming
dimensions in India. Addiction to alcohol? drugs not only affects the
individual involved, but also the family and society at large. India is
sandwiched between two largest opium producing regions of the world that is,
the Golden triangle comprising Thailand, Myanmar and Vietnam on one side, and
the Golden crescent comprising Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran on other. The
menace of drug /alcohol addiction has spread fast among the youth of India. As far as Tamil Nadu is concerned, the incidence of sale of
ganja and other narcotic drugs is increasing; and they are available very
easily near schools and colleges. Drug menace is rampant in Tamil Nadu, and
every day, there are reports of murders, as a result of drugs / alcohol abuse.
Drug and alcohol addiction has become a menace which threatens public health.
In Kallakurichi in Tamil Nadu, a month ago, more than 65
persons died due to consumption of illicit and spurious methanol mixed liquor.
I request the Centre to formulate a pan-India policy on drug / alcohol abuse,
and send an advisory to the States in order to reduce abuse of all types of
drugs.
(Ends)

records.title: Concern over problems faced by the Tamil Nadu fishermen.
Demand for Relief Package for the Flood-Affected people of Tamil Nadu.
details:
Dr. M. Thambidurai: Sir, on 18th
December, historic rains and subsequent flood paralysed normal life in
Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli, Tenkasi and Kanniyakumari districts of Tamil Nadu.
Unprecedented very heavy rainfall in these districts caused severe damage to
crops, properties and infrastructural facilities. These marooned districts had
been cut off from the rest of Tamil Nadu. Extensive damage to crops on thousands
of acres, and properties worth crores of rupees had taken place in these
districts. Several towns. and villages have been inundated. The infrastructure
roads, rail lines, canals, tanks and electric poles and many houses had been
affected. People had been worst affected and they are limping back to normal
life.
The Leader of the AIADMK
Party visited the affected people in those Districts and consoled them. There
is a dire need to provide them food, water and milk immediately. The Govt.
should immediately ensure rescue and relief measures. Our leader and former
Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu demanded that Rs 25,000 has to be given to each of
the affected farmers, and Rs.10 lakh should be given to the kin of each of
those who died in Tirunelveli. Based on the survey that he conducted, people
have been completely devastated. He has requested the Prime Minister to
consider peoples sufferings and provide sufficient relief funds.
Hence, I request the Central
Govt. to immediately sanction an amount of Rs. 15,000 crore to restore normal
life of the people of those districts.
(Ends)

records.title: Demand to give a stoppage of Shatabdi Express running between Chennai-Bengaluru (12027 and 12028) at Jolarpet.
details:
DR.
M. THAMBIDURAI (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I would like to bring the
following grievance of the people of Jolarpet to the kind attention of the hon.
Minister for a resolution. Jolarpet in Tamil Nadu is a major junction where the
footfall of the people is increasing day-by-day. Also, a new district was also
carved out consisting of Jolarpet. With massive increase in activities of the
people, they feel that there is a need for stoppage of a train at Jolarpet, to
cater to their daily needs. In this connection, I request him to kindly arrange
to give a stoppage of Shatabadi Express running between Chennai-Bengaluru
(12027 and 12028) at Jolarpet Junction, which is a major demand of the people
of Jolarpet. I request the hon. Minister to kindly look into the genuine
grievance of the people of Jolarpet and do the needful so that the Shatabadi
Express between Chennai and Bengaluru stops (both ways) at Jolarpet Junction.
Thank you very much. 
(Ends)

records.title: DEMAND FOR INSTALLATION OF DR. M.G. RAMACHANDRAN STATUE AT ENTRANCE OF CHENNAI CENTRAL RAILWAY STATION
details:
DR. M. THAMBIDURAI (TAMIL NADU): Mr. Deputy
Chairman, Sir, through you, I would like to bring to the notice of this august
House and the hon. Minister of Railways the following matter of urgent public
importance. Sir, as you know, Bharat Ratna, Puratchi Thalaivar, Dr. MGR was
the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu for three consecutive terms and he was a
respected leader not only in Tamil Nadu and India, but also in the entire
world. To pay respects to him and also to respect the sentiments of the Tamilians living all over the world, a request was made by
the AIADMK Party and the AIADMK Government earlier, to the Railway Ministry to
re-name the Chennai Central Railway Station as "Chennai MGR Railway
Station". This request was acceded to by the hon. Prime Minister and the
Railway Ministry, and subsequently, the name was changed. Now, it is only fit
and proper if the statue of Dr. MGR adorns the Railway Station. A request was
made already for the installation of his statue and for obtaining
NOC/permission for the same. I request, Sir, that necessary permission/NOC may
kindly be granted by the Railway Ministry for the installation of the statue of
Dr. Purathci Thalaivar MGR,
at the entrance of the Chennai Central Railway Station. Thank you for giving me
this opportunity. 
(Ends)

records.title: Demand for protecting the rights of Tamil Nadu in Cauvery River water share.
details:
DR. M
THAMBIDURAI (TAMIL NADU): Sir, I wish to bring to the notice of the
Government the need to protect the interest of Tamil Nadu in sharing Cauvery
water. Cauvery being an inter-State river, upper riparian States are not
permitted to construct any dam across Cauvery without the permission as
envisaged in the statutes. The proposal to construct Mekedatu
dam by Karnataka is of serious concern for Tamil Nadu. The proposed dam will impound
and divert flows from uncontrolled catchments to itself.
It is important to note that this component of flows from uncontrolled
catchments was taken into account by the Tribunal in the 2007 order while
arriving at the water allocation plan for the States. The annual water flows
from the catchments including the area between Kabini
dam in Karnataka and Billigundulu gauging site on the
inter-State border and the area between Krishnaraja Sagar dam in Karnataka and the gauging site will come to
naught if water is impounded by that dam. The Mekedatu
project also does not find mention in the Tribunal?s final order or the Supreme
Court judgement. The delta region known as the
granary of Tamil Nadu is immensely contributing to national foodgrain
production. Cauvery delta of Tamil Nadu that was once a prosperous agricultural
belt, has undergone drastic reduction in crop due to
reduced flow of water. The already water-deficient Cauvery delta of Tamil Nadu
will be worst hit by the proposed Mekedatu dam. I
urge upon the Government not to grant permission to Karnataka for constructing Mekedatu dam and protect the rights of Tamil Nadu. 
(Ends)
